title: Polynomial-size verifier circuits
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean-valued function of two finite Boolean lists, and let $p$ assign a natural number to each input length. There are natural numbers $a$ and $k$ such that, for every input length $n$ and every random-bit list $r$ of length $p(n)$, there is a well-formed fan-in-two directed acyclic Boolean circuit with $n$ inputs and size at most $a(n+1)^k$ that computes $M(v,r)$ on every input $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, with $v$ supplied as a list in its natural order.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean-valued function M on two Boolean lists
function p from natural numbers to natural numbers
random-bit list r has length p(n)
size at most a(n+1)^k for fixed natural numbers a and k
computation agrees with M on every Boolean input
